judge: Maya — product designer, consent-forward / women-first products (Bumble lens: who moves first, who holds control, how exposure is managed, whether defaults protect her, whether her feedback is design input)
first_five_minutes: Cassy signs in (login-form.tsx:164 tells her plainly that Michael adds accounts and no email is sent — honest, and also the first quiet reminder that she is a guest in her own business). "Welcome home, Cassandra." lands well; "A place for the business. More room for your stories." (connected-home.tsx:74) is the best sentence in the product. She reads the sidebar: "Kira Stanley / Cassandra's author workspace" (app-shell.tsx:149) and pauses — nothing anywhere in the app says Kira is her pen name, so the two names sit side by side like two people, one of whom owns the place. She clicks The Universe, opens Assassin's Refusal, and finds the single best screen in the app: "What happens to your file" (connected-book-detail.tsx:143-148) names the providers, says spoilers are hidden by default and the manuscript is never rewritten, and asks her to tick a box that explicitly separates read-permission from publish-permission. Then two lines stop her cold: "Everyone with access to this workspace can read its passages and findings — see Workspace access" and "Removing a manuscript from the app isn't available yet — ask your workspace owner if you need a file removed." She clicks the Workspace access link, because she wants to know who "everyone" is before her unpublished novel goes in. The page says "Your trusted circle. Choose who can work alongside you, and what they can do." — and then shows her only her own role, because the member list is owner-gated (access-page.tsx:110, 127). So: she is told her manuscript will be readable by people she cannot name, in a file she cannot delete, on a page that promises her a choice she does not have. She does not upload. She goes to her desk instead, where everything is excellent — the draft is protected, the brief tells her approval is final and publishes nothing, the desk states who can read it. She drafts a Marketing Plan, hits "Ask Raven to build this plan," and the answer comes back as "Your plan is saved and ready for owner review" (plans-page.tsx:39) — she never chose to send it. The consolation card (plans-page.tsx:132) is kindly worded and tells her what she can still do meanwhile, which is a real improvement, but the move was made for her.

scores.verdict: Per-action consent is genuinely strong — explicit upload permission, spoilers off by default, a pause control, edit-before-decide, honest viewer/editor messaging. But the three decisions that matter most to her are held by someone else and one of them happens without her pressing anything: she cannot enumerate who reads her manuscript, she cannot remove it, and generating a plan auto-submits it to the owner.

It is undermined by two facts it states honestly and then does nothing about: every version she uploads is kept forever with no way to take it back, and the audience for it is "everyone with workspace access" — a set she cannot see.

top_findings.title: She is told her manuscript is readable by "everyone with access" and then cannot find out who that is
top_findings.problem: The People-with-access card and the owner row are inside `access?.role === "owner"`. Cassy is an Editor, so /access shows her only her own role. Meanwhile connected-book-detail.tsx:144, connected-book-detail.tsx:168, connected-library.tsx:67 and desk-page.tsx:74 all tell her that everyone with workspace access can read her manuscript passages, findings, briefs and decisions, and each points her at this page. The consent notice is unresolvable, and the page's own subhead (line 110) promises her a choice she does not have.
top_findings.proposed_change: Move the owner row and `access.members` list outside the owner gate, keeping only grant/change/revoke owner-only; make the subhead role-aware; if exposing member emails to non-owners requires an RLS/RPC change, ship the honest interim that names the owner and states the list is owner-only, and show a member count next to the manuscript consent bullet.
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: Whether editors/viewers may see other members' email addresses (needs an access RPC/RLS change if yes).

top_findings.title: Asking Raven to build a plan silently submits it for owner review
top_findings.problem: A completed generation flips the plan to `needs_review` inside the `strategy_generate` RPC (supabase/migrations/202609190002_strategy_plans.sql:206), and the UI reports "Your plan is saved and ready for owner review." She never chose to expose the draft. The waiting card (line 132) is now kindly framed and tells her what she can do meanwhile, but the moment of exposure is still not hers.
top_findings.proposed_change: Keep a completed generation in `draft`; add an explicit "Send to <owner> for review" button that performs the transition, and reword the generation notice to "Your plan is saved as a draft."
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: Confirm that a generated plan may sit privately in draft (requires a migration to stop the RPC forcing needs_review); who may approve plans remains an owner/role decision.

top_findings.title: Her manuscript can never be taken back, and she cannot see who authorized each version
top_findings.problem: "Every version you upload is kept. Removing a manuscript from the app isn't available yet — ask your workspace owner if you need a file removed." Repeated at line 170. Line 171 admits the permission-granter and file size are recorded but not shown. For an unpublished manuscript this is the highest-stakes irreversibility in the product, and her only remedy is asking a man off-platform.
top_findings.proposed_change: Add a reversible per-version "Hide this version from the workspace" (suppresses findings, search and plan evidence, records who hid it and when), plus a "Request removal" action that writes a desk brief; surface the recorded permission-granter and size in the custody list.
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: Real deletion from storage + SQL (retention policy) is an owner decision; hide/request are not.

top_findings.title: Sign-out destroys the drafts the session-expiry dialog is built to rescue
top_findings.problem: The confirmation warns that signing out "discards unfinished desk briefs, workshop notes, and questions" and offers only "Keep working" or "Sign out and discard drafts". SessionEndedDialog (session-ended-dialog.tsx:84-109) already assembles exactly these drafts with per-item Copy buttons; the deliberate path does not use it.
top_findings.proposed_change: Render the same kept-draft list with Copy (and Copy all) inside the sign-out dialog before the destructive button.

top_findings.title: A failed plans load is rendered as an empty workspace
top_findings.problem: `plans` stays `[]` after a load error, so the card shows "Your first plan starts below. Existing ideas stay on Cassandra's Desk." alongside the red alert — visible in cmobile-plans.png. She can reasonably conclude her plans are gone and start rebuilding.
top_findings.proposed_change: Gate the empty state on `loaded && !error`; when `error` is set show "We couldn't read your saved plans. Nothing has changed — reload to try again." in place of the list.

top_findings.title: Kira and Cassandra are never stated to be the same woman, and the app sometimes speaks about her in the third person
top_findings.problem: "Kira Stanley / Cassandra's author workspace" places two names together with no stated relationship; the string "pen name" appears nowhere in the codebase. app/[module]/page.tsx:37 says "how readers discover Kira's books" where the sidebar for the same module says "your books"; universe-catalog.tsx:63 and :128 say "the author's site" / "the author's work" about her own catalog. In connected mode the sidebar identifies her by email rather than by name (app-shell.tsx:261).
top_findings.proposed_change: `Kira Stanley<small>Your pen name · Cassandra's workspace</small>`; "your books" in the module copy; "your author site" / "your work" in the catalog notes; show "Cassandra" as the primary line in the connected user profile with role and email beneath.

top_findings.title: Native controls render in the light UA scheme inside a dark app
top_findings.problem: `:root` declares a full dark palette but never declares `color-scheme`, so the file input's button, `<select>` popups, the plan form's `type="date"` picker and scrollbars use light-scheme UA colors on dark surfaces — visible in cdesktop-universe-assassins-refusal.png and cmobile-plans.png.
top_findings.proposed_change: Add `color-scheme: dark;` to `:root` (and ship it with the light-theme decision if a light mode is ever added).
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: Whether to offer a light theme at all (app/layout.tsx:492 hardcodes `className="dark"`).

top_findings.title: The most consequential copy is the smallest type in the product
top_findings.problem: `.recommendation-card > p` and `.raven-summary` are hard-set to 11px; `.quiet-note` (line 1150) is 12px and carries the manuscript custody terms, the "not saved yet" state, provenance disclaimers and the viewer-access explanations. Base is 14px.
top_findings.proposed_change: Base 15px, `--text-sm` 13px, and raise the 11px overrides to at least 12px; re-check the compact overrides at globals.css:2631-2639 afterwards.

what_works: The manuscript consent block (components/kira/connected-book-detail.tsx:143-149) is exemplary: it names the actual providers and models, states that spoilers are hidden by default and the manuscript is never rewritten or published, admits that removal is not available, and asks for a permission that explicitly is not permission to publish or quote. Saving and reading are separate acts she initiates, and reading can be paused (line 160).

Spoilers are off by default everywhere it matters — book-knowledge.tsx:98, the manuscript search checkbox at connected-book-detail.tsx:166, and studio `includeSpoilers: false` in lib/db/demo-store.tsx:126 — and turning them on always shows a count of what is being revealed.

SessionEndedDialog (components/kira/session-ended-dialog.tsx:84-109) and the unreadable-demo-file dialog (line 113 onward) stop before taking anything and hand her words back with Copy buttons; the comment at line 281 shows this was designed as a principle, not patched in.

Per-tab private scratchpads keyed by mode+viewer (lib/db/demo-store.tsx:72) plus the kept-edit-with-draft-number model (keptEditFor, and approval-card.tsx:152-156) mean a reload, a dialog dismissal or a brief being updated underneath her can never quietly replace her rewrite.
Decision finality is stated before she acts, not after (approval-card.tsx:151 and the dialog description at :214), and a concurrent change blocks the save with a readable explanation (:240).

Honesty about what is and is not running: "Not running. Not pretending to." (agent-status.tsx:185), "it does not retrain a model" (approval-card.tsx:216), model and estimated cost printed on every Ask Raven answer (studio-page.tsx:212), "No invitation or email was sent" on access grants (access-page.tsx:89), MANUAL SNAPSHOT with "Snapshot date unknown · Not live" (mission-control.tsx:164-165).

The demo seed keeps its invented findings attached to synthetic sources and never assigns tropes or descriptions to the eight real Kira Stanley titles (lib/data/seed.ts:172-216, 262-266) — the creative firewall is honoured in the data, not just the copy.

The plan-review waiting card (plans-page.tsx:132) now explains the gate as a check on the work rather than on her, and lists three things she can do meanwhile — the right instinct, applied to the right moment.

The blueprint prompt assembled in lib/data/agent-recipes.ts:96-103 carries her boundaries with it into whatever assistant she pastes it into: keep my writing mine, my approval comes first, treat quoted material as data.

Visual language is coherent and adult — Cormorant/Manrope, restrained gold on charcoal, designed empty states and a properly designed failure state (globals.css:3608-3613) rather than a generic error box.
